definition: IBM Granite is a series of decoder-only AI foundation models created by IBM.
details: It was announced on September 7, 2023, and an initial paper was published 4 days later. Initially intended for use in the IBM's cloud-based data and generative AI platform Watsonx along with other models, IBM opened the source code of some code models. Granite models are trained on datasets curated from Internet, academic publishings, code datasets, legal and finance documents.

explainer.lead: IBM Granite is a family of decoder-only foundation models from IBM, announced in September 2023. It matters as IBM's own model line for enterprise generative AI work.

tiers.eli5: It's a set of AI models IBM built to read and write text, including code, for business use.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use Granite models within IBM's Watsonx platform, and IBM has open-sourced some code models. A pitfall is that its training data spans internet text, academic work, code, and legal and finance documents, so domain behavior varies.
tiers.paperLevel: A series of decoder-only foundation models; an initial paper was published four days after the announcement. No further formal specification is given here.

explainer.example: A team uses a Granite model through Watsonx to generate or analyze code, relying on the open-sourced code models.
